A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same resource-constrained federated continual learning benchmark. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and v2 appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, resource ablations, technique comparisons, and task-count and task-order sensitivity results in Tables II and IV and Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Tables 2–4 and Figures 1–3, including revised FOT results in the task-order comparison.

M1.justification: The benchmark retains the same method components and adaptations, including inference without supplied task identities for FOT and FedWeIT. Rewritten descriptions and relocated baseline explanations do not establish algorithmic changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet for class-incremental learning, and Digit-10, Office-31, and Office-Caltech-10 for domain-incremental learning. Additional applications mentioned in v2 Appendix A are related work, not new evaluations.

E2.justification: The twelve-method sufficient-resource comparison and five-method extremely limited-resource comparison retain identical comparator membership in v1 Table II and v2 Tables 2–3. Comparator sets in Figures 1–3 and the reversed-order table also remain unchanged; FCIL/GLFC wording refers to the same cited method.

E3.justification: v1 Table III and v2 Table 5 contain identical experimental settings, including task and client counts, partition parameters, metrics, batch sizes, learning rates, rounds, and resource budgets. The backbone exceptions and sensitivity-test conditions are also retained.

E4.justification: Both retain the same resource ablations, technique analyses, task-count sensitivity study, and reversed-domain-order test. Their questions and tested conditions are unchanged; the FOT numerical revisions within the retained task-order analysis are assessed under E6.

E5.justification: Both specify two runs per setting and use each run's final ten rounds to calculate the average and what the text calls standard variance. The uncertainty-reporting procedure is unchanged; revised FOT means and accompanying uncertainty values do not establish additional runs or a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Four FOT entries change between v1 Table IV and v2 Table 4. Reversed-order Digit-10 final/average accuracy changes from 76.85±0.74/85.44±0.83 to 74.45±0.82/83.91±0.76; Office-31 changes from 42.25±0.79/45.11±0.62 to 40.29±0.94/43.86±0.73. These revisions alter some reported rankings. Other result-table entries and the plotted content of Figures 1–3 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The FL and FCL objectives in Equations 1–2 and the class/domain-incremental definitions move from v1 Section II-A to v2 Appendix B without substantive mathematical changes. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: benchmarking three resource constraints, demonstrating existing FCL methods' resource dependence, analyzing common techniques, and identifying future research directions.

C2.justification: v2 Section 3.2 replaces v1's explanation that Re-Fed combines generated and real data with an explanation centered on handling data heterogeneity, consistent with its retained baseline description. The condensed technique conclusion also strengthens knowledge distillation from a 'viable and efficient alternative' to 'optimal under constraints' without additional experiments. Most limitations and future recommendations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies Huazhong University of Science and Technology's HPC platform as the computation facility. GPU types and counts, optimizer, schedule, hyperparameters, and references to baseline implementations otherwise remain unchanged or are relocated to Appendix B.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive Background and Related Work appendix covering heterogeneous FL, continual-learning method families, and FCL assumptions and applications. New discussions include federated distillation, multi-granularity prompting, traceable FCL, incremental segmentation, and intrusion detection, substantially expanding the earlier introduction's research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the manuscript: problem formulation and detailed dataset/baseline descriptions move to Appendix B, future directions move to Appendix C, and a new background appendix is added. Several passages are rewritten or condensed, author biographies are removed, and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column IEEE layout to a single-column conference layout. Table II's panels become separate Tables 2 and 3, the settings table moves to Appendix B, and Figure 3 and Table 4 are arranged side by side. Figures and tables are substantially rescaled, although the scientific plots themselves are reused unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix A provides useful context about FL, continual learning, and earlier FCL assumptions, while Section 3.2 removes the internally inconsistent explanation of Re-Fed as combining generated and real data. These yield a modest improvement in exposition. Smaller displays and the less-qualified claim that distillation is 'optimal under constraints' temper the benefit. The unexplained FOT revisions do not establish improved experimental validity, and the main evidence remains unchanged.
